title: Old Bangalore, early
kicker: Temples, dosas and a flower market
note: Start before the city wakes. A rock, a temple, two legendary tiffin rooms and the best flower market in India, all within a few kilometres.

title: The colonial core
note: The city's civic heart on foot: a park, a red-brick courthouse, a library, a cathedral and a very old restaurant.

title: Museum mile, rain or shine
note: When the clouds open, head for the museums. Art, engines, a dinosaur and a quiet garden, with coffee at the end.

title: Malleshwaram tiffin & tanks
kicker: Dosas, a temple and a lake
note: A north-Bengaluru morning: two tiffin institutions, an old market, a violin-shaped concert hall and a sunset lake.

title: Indiranagar cafe crawl
note: A slow afternoon in the east: podi idli, boutiques, a bookshop and a brewery. Ends at Toit, so you can have the second beer.

title: Lakes at golden hour
note: A cab loop from north to central Bengaluru, timed for the light. Pick one lake to linger at; the others are for the drive.

title: Frazer Town flavours
note: A walkable pocket of the cantonment with the city's best khova naan, a late-night roll shop and a proper biryani room.

title: Garden city green loop
note: Two of the city's great gardens, a rocky park and a market street. A half-day of green with a tiffin stop in the middle.

title: Nandi Hills at sunrise
note: Leave at 4:30am, climb before the sun, then come down for temple stonework and a fort gate. Back in the city by lunch.

stops.name: Nandi Hills
stops.note: Sunrise above the clouds; go on a weekday if you can.

stops.name: Bhoga Nandeeshwara Temple
stops.note: A 9th-century temple with exquisite stonework at the foot of the hill.

stops.name: Devanahalli Fort
stops.note: Tipu Sultan's birthplace, a quiet fort with a grassy moat.

title: Mysore in a day
note: An early start on the expressway, the palace before the crowds, a market walk and a temple on the hill. Long, but worth it.

stops.name: Mysore Palace
stops.note: Go at opening; the durbar hall and the painted ceiling are the highlight.

stops.name: Devaraja Market
stops.note: Flowers, kumkum and produce in a lovely old market hall.

stops.name: Chamundeshwari Temple
stops.note: A hilltop temple with a view over the city.

stops.name: Srirangapatna
stops.note: An island fort town on the way back, with Tipu's summer palace and a river ghat.

title: Rocks & river country
note: Granite hills, a river gorge and a waterfall. Start early; the rocks get hot by noon.

stops.name: Ramanagara
stops.note: The silk town and the rocky hills behind it; a good first stop for breakfast.

stops.name: Savandurga
stops.note: One of Asia's largest monoliths; the climb is steep but the view is enormous.

stops.name: Manchanabele Dam
stops.note: A quiet reservoir below the hills, good for a picnic.

stops.name: Chunchi Falls
stops.note: A seasonal waterfall on the Arkavathi; check the water before you go.

title: Dance villages & silence
note: A slower day out: a classical dance village, a meditation pyramid and a spiritual campus. Carry water and an open mind.

stops.name: Nrityagram
stops.note: A dance village founded by Protima Bedi; check performance dates before visiting.

stops.name: Pyramid Valley
stops.note: A meditation centre with a large pyramid and quiet grounds.

stops.name: Art of Living International Center
stops.note: A vast campus on the Kanakapura Road with gardens and a lake.

title: Bannerghatta, wild and slow
note: A national park, a butterfly enclosure and two quiet roads beyond it. Start at the gate before the buses arrive, then let the afternoon go loose.

stops.name: Bannerghatta National Park
stops.note: The safari gate opens early; book the first slot and keep an eye on the canopy.

stops.name: Butterfly Park
stops.note: A small enclosed garden of butterflies beside the zoo — good with children.

stops.name: Ragihalli Forest
stops.note: Scrub forest and back roads; go with a local guide and carry water.

stops.name: Muthyalamaduvu
stops.note: A seasonal waterfall in Anekal taluk — check the water before making the detour.

title: Shivagange, above the silk road
note: A steep granite hill, a temple at its foot and two stops on the old northern road. The climb is short and sharp; the views are the point.

stops.name: Shivagange Peak
stops.note: A steep climb on stone steps; start early and carry water. Monkeys are bold.

stops.name: Shivagange Garbhagudi
stops.note: The cave shrine at the base, busy with pilgrims on weekends.

stops.name: Bhoga Nandeeshwara Temple
stops.note: A 9th-century temple complex with fine stonework and quiet courtyards.

stops.name: Devanahalli Fort
stops.note: Tipu Sultan's birthplace: a low fort, a grassy moat and almost no crowd.

title: Devarayanadurga, hill and spring
note: A hill temple, a spring that never stops, and a forest on the way home. A good first day trip if you want the road without the crowds.

stops.name: Devarayanadurga Hill
stops.note: A granite hill with a temple on top and a long view north of the city.

stops.name: Namada Chilume
stops.note: A spring beside the road, named for the mark Rama is said to have left.

stops.name: Bhoga Narasimha Temple
stops.note: The older temple at the foot of the hill, with a stepped tank.

stops.name: Turahalli Forest
stops.note: A scrub-and-rock forest on the city edge; a soft landing on the way back.

title: Srirangapatna & the river
note: An island fort town, a bird sanctuary and a formal garden at the end of the day. Leave before dawn and you will beat the Mysore Road traffic.

stops.name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
stops.note: Boat rides under the trees; best in the first hour after opening.

stops.name: Srirangapatna Fort
stops.note: Tipu's island capital: walls, a mosque and the summer palace.

stops.name: Nimishamba Temple
stops.note: A riverside temple on the Cauvery, a few minutes from the fort.

stops.name: Brindavan Gardens
stops.note: Terraced gardens below the KRS dam; stay for the evening lights if you can.
